models_evaluated: six LLMs (not named in the text)

links.outcome: LLM triage agreement (QWK) on completed records versus sequential checkpoints
links.effect: All six LLMs fell from moderate-to-substantial agreement on completed records to fair-to-moderate at every sequential checkpoint. Best model QWK was 0.295 versus 0.887-0.929 for three expert clinicians.
links.quote: Deploying LLMs for ED triage based on offline benchmarks alone misses this sequential failure.

links.outcome: Standalone LLM triage performance compared with clinician performance on the same conversations
links.effect: Three expert clinicians reached a QWK of 0.887-0.929 on the same conversations, while the best model reached 0.295.
links.quote: Three expert clinicians on the same conversations reach a QWK of 0.887-0.929, while the best model reaches 0.295.

links.outcome: LLM triage sensitivity to input variation via controlled perturbations and prompting interventions
links.effect: Controlled perturbations showed labels at every checkpoint were anchored on the chief complaint exchanges. Prompting interventions failed to lift the plateau.
links.quote: Controlled perturbations show that the label at every checkpoint is anchored on the chief complaint exchanges, and prompting interventions fail to lift this plateau.

links.outcome: LLM ESI acuity prediction distribution and agreement with ground truth
links.effect: Predictions concentrated at ESI-2 and ESI-3. Models agreed with each other more than with ground truth, so ensembling worsened the failure.
links.quote: Predictions concentrate at ESI-2 and ESI-3, and models agree with each other more than with the ground truth, so ensembling worsens the failure.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating LLMs on sequential, turn-by-turn prefixes rather than completed retrospective records
Ensembling multiple LLMs as a mitigation (found to worsen the failure)

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of LLM performance on sequential emergency triage conversations versus complete records, testing prompting interventions and warning against deploying based on static benchmarks.

primary.practice: sequential vs static evaluation and prompting interventions
